item.title: Meiji Mura: A Village of Japan's Modernising Age — Guide
item.description: Meiji Mura is one of Japan’s great open-air museums, preserving more than 60 authentic buildings of the Meiji era (1868–1912) — the tumultuous age when Japan flung open its doors and hybridised Western brick, clapboard and stained glass with its own carpentry. Rescued from demolition across the country and rebuilt on a wooded hillside above Lake Iruka near Inuyama, the collection ranges from churches, post offices and a kabuki theatre to its crown jewel, the reconstructed main entrance hall of Frank Lloyd Wright’s Imperial Hotel, while a working steam locomotive and vintage Kyoto trams carry visitors between the districts.

item.title: Iwate Bank Red Brick Building: Morioka's Meiji Landmark — Guide
item.description: The Iwate Bank Red Brick Building is one of Morioka’s best-loved landmarks — a handsome 1911 former bank designed by Kingo Tatsuno, architect of Tokyo Station, and his partner. Its red brick and white stone facade anchors the historic city centre, and the beautifully restored interior is open to visitors. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Morioka, Iwate Hours ~10:00–16:30 (closed Tue) Admission Around ¥300 (interior) Time needed About 40 min Best time Year-round What to See The red brick and white stone Meiji facade (1911).
